item.title: Ratko Mladic, ex-Bosnian Serb warlord who oversaw atrocities, has died at 84
item.description: Ratko Mladic was one of the most notorious figures of a war that killed over 100,000 people in the 1990s. He commanded his troops to "scorch the brains" of the Bosnian Muslims and boasted of being a "Serbian God."
item.content:encoded:
Ratko Mladic was one of the most notorious figures of a war that killed over 100,000 people in the 1990s. He commanded his troops to "scorch the brains" of the Bosnian Muslims and boasted of being a "Serbian God."

(Image credit: Peter Dejong)

item.title: Meta reaches $17B settlement. And, nuclear regulator to abandon radiation safety rule
item.description: Meta and the states that sued the company have agreed to a $17 billion settlement. And, nuclear regulators are preparing to abandon a decades-old radiation safety rule.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Floods kill nearly 400 people in Nepal and Tibet, with 90 Americans among the missing
item.description: Many of the missing are foreign tourists after deadly floods hit the Nepal-Tibet border, sweeping away entire villages.

item.title: Official leading Trump's Gaza ceasefire effort criticizes Israel for its attacks
item.description: The official in charge of President Trump's ceasefire plan for Gaza criticized Israel for its attacks on the Palestinian territory and warned that the alternative to the U.S. proposal is the next war.

item.title: Yayoi Kusama, high priestess of polka dots, has died
item.description: The Japanese artist has died at age 97. Kusama's polka dotted pumpkins, "Infinity Rooms," and other repetitive and dreamlike artworks have been shown in museums and galleries worldwide.

item.title: Greetings from Karbala, Iraq, where millions gathered for a Shia pilgrimage
item.description: Pilgrims came to Iraq from all over the world in August. Many Iraqi and Iranian pilgrims walked hundreds of miles in extreme heat to mark the event. Outside the shrines, the atmosphere is almost festive.

item.title: Nearly 1,000 are missing in Nepal and Tibet after floods caused by a glacial collapse
item.description: China's Xinhua News Agency said Thursday that mudslides in Tibet caused by a glacial collapse have left three people dead and 558 missing, while police in Nepal reported at least 162 were killed.
item.content:encoded:
China's Xinhua News Agency said Thursday that mudslides in Tibet caused by a glacial collapse have left three people dead and 558 missing, while police in Nepal reported at least 162 were killed.

(Image credit: Niranjan Shrestha)

item.title: Canada to hit U.S. with retaliatory tariffs. And, remembering music legend Dolly Parton
item.description: Canada has announced it plans to hit the U.S. with countertariffs that mirror its actions "dollar for dollar." And, remembering the legacy of country star and icon Dolly Parton, who died at 80.

item.title: Hospital nursery fire kills 14 newborns in Pakistan's capital, officials order immediate inquiry
item.description: A fire erupted early Wednesday in a nursery for newborns at a major government hospital in Pakistan's capital, killing 14 babies, according to hospital officials and the government.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: More than 50 kidnapped as violent gang attack in Haiti leaves 47 dead
item.description: It is believed to be one of the largest mass kidnappings in Haiti in recent years, and one gang leader is threatening to kill the hostages if authorities kill any gang members as they try to secure the community nestled in the hills above Port-au-Prince.
